title: One operation is a span
intro: A span records one operation, including its start, duration and attributes. It describes observed execution rather than the intended plan.
takeaway: Instrumentation creates spans. Missing instrumentation means some operations will not appear.

beats.text: The caller invokes a remote test tool. That operation takes time.
Instrumentation records the start. The tool performs its work.
The operation ends and its span closes. The record includes duration and outcome.
This span describes one operation. Several related spans can form a trace.

title: Related spans form a trace
intro: A trace groups related spans. They share a trace ID but each has its own span ID. Parent IDs describe the nesting relationship.
takeaway: Shared trace identity links operations; distinct span identities keep individual work identifiable.

beats.text: The agent operation starts trace T. Its children represent individual calls.
A model call gets its own span ID. It keeps trace T and the parent relation.
A tool call gets another span ID. It also belongs to trace T.
The trace view groups the related spans. Parent links show how they fit together.

title: Cross a service boundary
intro: When an operation crosses a process boundary, tracing context must travel with the request and be extracted by the receiving service.
takeaway: Propagation links the spans, but instrumentation and export must also work. Headers alone do not create a complete trace.

beats.text: The agent calls a separate service. A local parent relation cannot cross alone.
Include trace context in the request. It identifies the trace and parent span.
The receiver extracts that context. It starts a child span for its work.
Both sides now share trace identity. Export their spans to see the whole path.

title: Visibility is not a speedup
intro: In this illustrative sequential run, the model takes 0.6 seconds and the tool 2.4 seconds. Correct propagation makes the slow tool visible but does not shorten the work.
takeaway: Use tracing to locate time. A tracing repair is an observability improvement, not automatically a performance optimization.

beats.text: Example: two calls run sequentially. 0.6 + 2.4 = 3.0 seconds total.
Without linkage, the tool looks separate. Its time is harder to attribute.
Next run: propagate the request context. Export now links the same 2.4s tool span.
The run still takes 3.0 seconds. We improved visibility, not execution speed.

title: Missing and sensitive data
intro: Sampling, export failures and missing instrumentation can omit spans. Recorded attributes can also contain sensitive information unless the application controls them.
takeaway: A missing span is not proof that work never happened. Minimize sensitive attributes and treat traces as partial evidence.

beats.text: Runtime operations produce tracing data. Not every detail should be recorded.
Remove a secret attribute from span A. Keep the span itself in the export.
Separately, span B fails to export. The view has A, but B is missing.
Use traces with their collection limits. Absence of a span is not proof of absence.
